status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: Moltbook secured the issue within hours and Wiz reports deleting the research data. The provider repaired the identified exposure, without proving that all prior access or possible misuse was discovered.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The unsecured backend exposed email addresses and private messages to researchers without authority. This failed to protect the privacy of affected platform participants.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: Researchers obtained unauthorised read-and-write access to the agent platform’s private communications and authentication tokens through an unsecured backend. The platform did not preserve its security boundary. Token misuse or impersonation is not established.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence is a large-scale data and credential exposure caused by a backend security misconfiguration. The evidence does not establish that an AI model made the configuration decision or that a current VIGIL Failure Class is the right mechanism abstraction. Backend access, private information, exposed-token capabilities and remediation remain distinct. No token misuse, agent impersonation or AI-side permission inference is established; technical vulnerability alone does not force a taxonomy mechanism.
conclusion_change.new: The agent platform exposed private data and credentials through a backend misconfiguration. Security and privacy failed, while repair of the identified issue is supported. The evidence does not attribute the configuration decision to an AI model or establish token misuse.
